summary: Phase S3 security and boundary re-audit passes at the remediation baseline through 40a9e3b3. The Drizzle adapter is permanently bound to an authenticated school and actor, performs all database work through a lazily cached real TenantDB, derives request and result digests inside the trusted boundary, and returns provider-neutral typed failures. Composite database constraints now prevent cross-school user, card, review, evidence, state, placement, and commit ownership violations; the frozen placement and calibration natural uniqueness contracts are restored; and the reconstructed 0026/0027 snapshots plus additive 0028 preflight migration form a contiguous, test-verified ledger without introducing a db-to-domain dependency.
nonblocking_findings: Infrastructure - Live migration-ledger verification is unavailable because neither DIRECT_DATABASE_URL nor DATABASE_URL is configured. Offline Drizzle validation, the committed ledger/snapshot tests, and PGlite execution of migrations through 0028 all pass.

Infrastructure/coordination - A literal clean-worktree drizzle-kit generate was not used as acceptance evidence because committed packages/db/src/schema/primary.ts still trails the already-present unrelated working-tree NOT NULL correction introduced by 0026. Phase S3 instead has a deterministic terminal-snapshot-to-current-mastery-metadata proxy and drizzle-kit check; the unrelated primary.ts drift must remain with its owning work rather than be absorbed into this track.

Test diagnostics - The PGlite domain tests print the existing DATABASE_URL-not-set warning while importing the DB package, but execute entirely against their injected PGlite database and pass. This warning is not a failed query or a mastery boundary bypass.
evidence: The adapter constructor rejects a null tenant or blank actor, binds schoolId and actorId once, rejects every foreign-school operation or audit-actor mismatch before mutation, and creates/caches createTenantDB(db, { schoolId }) for reads and serializable transactions.

TenantDB wraps transaction callbacks as TenantDB instances, injects or validates schoolId on every FLAT insert, and scopes select/update/delete builders; all seven mastery tables remain registered FLAT.

Drizzle schema metadata and 0028 SQL contain composite (school_id, student_id) ownership FKs for cards, states, placements, and commits, plus composite owner-chain FKs for reviews to cards and evidence to reviews. The supporting users, card, and review composite unique constraints are present.

Physical PGlite adversarial tests reject a school-A row referencing a school-B user, reject review/card and evidence/review owner mismatches, prevent referenced owner retargeting, enforce parent-before-child writes, and prove rollback after a later FK failure.

The public command schema validates UUID-backed record IDs and strict school/student self-consistency. The adapter canonicalizes the parsed command, computes its own lowercase sha256 request digest, derives a distinct result digest, stores both inside the immutable receipt, and detects same-key changed-payload conflicts without trusting caller-supplied digest fields.

Placement uniqueness is restored on (schoolId, studentId, objectiveId, graphRelease, evidenceType), and calibration uniqueness on (schoolId, domain, ageBand, paramsVersion), across schema metadata, 0028 SQL, terminal snapshot, and live PGlite tests.

Snapshots 0026, 0027, and 0028 are tracked and form the exact 0025 -> 0026 -> 0027 -> 0028 prevId chain. Mastery is absent at 0026, all seven tables appear at 0027, and 0028 adds only hardening constraints after a non-destructive fail-closed ownership and duplicate-key preflight.
The 0028 preflight preserves invalid legacy rows and applies no constraints when ownership validation fails; it contains no mastery DELETE or UPDATE repair path.

Provider errors map to stable MasteryPersistenceError codes and retryability without leaking provider messages: serialization/connection, timeout, missing migration, append-only conflict, and unexpected internal failure are covered.

A focused source scan found no @reading-advantage/domain import in the DB-owned mastery schema, physical tenant tests, migration-repro tests, ledger doctor, or migration SQL. Drizzle/provider imports remain confined to the dedicated Domain adapter boundary.
